facts.name: Lanceleaf Coreopsis
facts.notes: Cheerful yellow flowers from late spring into summer; cut back spent stems for more blooms. Thrives in poor, dry soil.

sources.title: Michigan Wildflower Farm: Dryland species list
sources.note: Michigan seed grower; marks any species that is not native to Michigan.

sources.title: University of Nebraska Extension: Early Summer Maintenance for Perennials
sources.note: Shear perennial salvia, coreopsis, Shasta daisy, columbine, coral bells, hardy geranium and catmint after flowering; many rebloom in 5 to 6 weeks.

companions.why: Combines with yellow flowers such as coreopsis and goldenrod, pink ones such as purple coneflower, prairie grasses and silver plants such as Stachys (lamb's ear).

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Blazing Star article

companions.why: Combine with Penstemon 'Husker Red' or purple speedwells; works well with coreopsis, purple coneflower, blazing star, black-eyed Susan, little bluestem and prairie dropseed.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Butterfly Weed article

companions.why: Combines well with beebalm and Shasta daisies; harmonizes with yellow foxglove, Coreopsis and lemon daylilies.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Catmint 'Walker's Low' article

companions.why: Combined with fall-blooming sedums; a great filler between purple coneflower, liatris, black-eyed Susan and butterfly weed.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Prairie Dropseed article

companions.why: Walters Gardens (Zeeland, Michigan) lists varieties of these as companions: Liatris and Coreopsis.

sources.title: Walters Gardens, Zeeland, Michigan: Sea Holly companions

companions.why: Izel Native Plants: plant wild strawberry intermingled with lanceleaf coreopsis and purple coneflower.
New Moon Nurseries: in lightly shaded gardens, companions include wild columbine, Pennsylvania sedge and lanceleaf coreopsis.
